_comment: Low-back / core corridor — non-specific low-back pain and post-flare rehab, McGill- and McKenzie-informed; authored in-house (original instruction text; exercise mechanics are facts, phrasing is ours).

exercises.name: Pelvic Tilt
instructions: Lie on your back with both knees bent and feet flat on the floor, arms resting at your sides.
Gently tighten your abdominals to roll the pelvis back, flattening the small of your back toward the floor.
Hold the position while breathing normally — the movement is subtle, and your hips stay on the floor.
Release slowly and let the natural curve of your back return before the next tilt.

exercises.name: Single Knee-to-Chest
instructions: Lie on your back with both knees bent and feet flat.
Bring one knee up and grasp behind the thigh with both hands.
Draw the knee gently toward your chest until you feel an easy stretch in the lower back and buttock — a steady pull, never a bounce.
Hold while the other foot stays relaxed on the floor, then lower the leg with control and switch sides.

exercises.name: Lower-Trunk Rotation
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and together, feet flat, arms out to the sides for balance.
Keeping the knees stacked, slowly lower them toward one side as far as comfortable.
Let both shoulders stay heavy on the floor — the twist comes from the trunk, not the arms.
Bring the knees back to center with control, then repeat toward the other side.

exercises.name: Cat-Camel
instructions: Start on hands and knees, hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Slowly round your back up toward the ceiling, letting your head drop gently.
Then reverse: let the belly sink as the chest and tailbone lift, eyes coming forward.
Glide between the two shapes through a comfortable range — this is a motion drill, not a stretch, so stay well short of strain.

exercises.name: Prone Press-Up
instructions: Lie face down with your hands flat beside your shoulders, elbows bent.
Press through your hands to lift your chest, letting the back arch while the hips and thighs stay relaxed on the floor.
Straighten the elbows only as far as comfortable, breathing out as you rise.
Lower back down slowly. Stop if symptoms spread farther down your leg — pain drawing in toward the spine is the pattern you want.

exercises.name: Dead Bug
instructions: Lie on your back with arms pointing at the ceiling and hips and knees bent to 90 degrees, shins level like a tabletop.
Gently brace your midsection so the lower back stays quiet against the floor.
Slowly lower one arm overhead and the opposite leg toward the floor, only as far as the back can stay still.
Return to the start and repeat with the other arm-and-leg pair — slow beats big.

exercises.name: Modified Curl-Up
instructions: Lie on your back with one knee bent and the other leg straight; slide both hands under the small of your back, palms down, to support its natural curve.
Lift your head and shoulders as one unit just a short way off the floor — the neck stays long and the low back does not flatten onto your hands.
Hold briefly while breathing, then lower back down without letting the back curve change.
Swap which knee is bent partway through so both sides share the work.

exercises.name: Standing Hip Hinge
instructions: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and knees soft, holding a dowel upright along your spine — or place one hand on your breastbone and the other on your belly.
Push your hips straight back, letting the chest tip forward like a drawbridge while the back stays long.
Keep the dowel touching the back of your head, upper back, and tailbone the whole way — or keep the distance between your hands unchanged.
Hinge only as far as the hamstrings allow without the back rounding, then drive the hips forward to stand tall.

exercises.name: Bird Dog
instructions: Start on hands and knees, hands under shoulders and knees under hips, back in its natural neutral curve.
Reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back until both are level with your trunk.
Hold steady — pelvis level and low back quiet, as if a full cup were balanced on it.
Return to all fours with control, then repeat with the opposite pair.

exercises.name: Side Plank (Knees)
instructions: Lie on your side propped on your forearm, elbow under the shoulder, knees bent and stacked; a folded towel under the bottom knee adds comfort.
Lift your hips forward and up until your body forms a straight line from head to knees.
Keep the hips pressed forward — don't let them sag toward the floor or drift behind you.
Hold while breathing normally, then lower with control and switch sides.

exercises.name: Side Plank
instructions: Lie on your side propped on your forearm, elbow under the shoulder, legs straight with the feet stacked or staggered.
Lift the hips until the body forms one straight line from ear to ankle.
Keep the shoulders and hips stacked vertically — no rolling forward or back.
Hold while breathing normally; lower the moment the line begins to sag, then switch sides.

progressions.note: Progress once you can hold the tilt through several slow breaths without the hips lifting or the legs tensing.
Move to quadruped once opposite arm-and-leg reps stay slow with the lower back motionless throughout.
Add the hold once the full glide is smooth and symptom-free through the whole comfortable range.
Add rotation once each knee draws to the chest through full range with nothing felt down the leg.
Layer in the curl-up once you can find and keep the neutral curve while breathing quietly.
Add lateral work once curl-up reps stay smooth with the neck relaxed and no change felt at the hands under the back.
Straighten the legs once the knee version holds a steady line on both sides without the hips sagging.
Take the drill to standing once you can set the neutral curve on the first try and keep it while breathing quietly.
